page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Optimized3.36 is a bare metal server configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. The platform features an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, providing 36 physical cores and 72 dedicated vCPUs using two threads per core. System memory totals 512.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 7.11 GB per vCPU. Because this is a bare metal instance, there is no hypervisor layer, giving the operating system direct access to all compute and memory resources.

The server incorporates 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage integrated directly onto the host, accommodating workloads that demand high local disk throughput. It operates without discrete graphics accelerators, containing zero GPUs. Network provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated allocation of cores and direct hardware access eliminates resource contention from noisy neighbors.

Given its 3.0 GHz Intel Xeon processing cores, large 512.0 GB memory capacity, and direct-attached NVMe storage, this server fits workloads requiring sustained compute throughput and low-latency storage access. Relevant applications include high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, large-scale ETL pipelines, and continuous integration compilation jobs.
